title: Printable coordinate grid sheet (lesson 54)
subject: Mathematics
unit: Summer 1: Enlargement and similarity; ratio and proportion; rates
source: Seeded from mathematics/y9 lesson 54 (Printable coordinate grid sheet (portal worksheet for this lesson))
intro: Lesson 54: Describing enlargements: finding the centre and scale factor. To understand how to describe an enlargement fully by finding its scale factor and centre

model.title: Object (1, 1), (2, 1), (1, 3) has image (3, 1), (5, 1), (3, 5). Describe the transformation fully.

parts.label: Step 1
parts.text: Side from (1, 1) to (2, 1) is 1; its image is 2: scale factor 2

parts.label: Step 2
parts.text: Ray lines through (1, 1) and (3, 1), and through (1, 3) and (3, 5)

questions.q: Object (2, 2), (4, 2), (2, 3) has image (4, 4), (8, 4), (4, 6). Describe the transformation fully.
questions.model: Lengths double: scale factor 2. Every image coordinate is double the object's, so the ray lines meet at the origin.

questions.q: Object (6, 6), (9, 6), (6, 9) has image (2, 2), (3, 2), (2, 3). Describe it fully.
A perimeter of 12 cm becomes 30 cm. Scale factor?

questions.a: (a) enlargement, scale factor 2, centre (0, 0) (b) enlargement, scale factor 3, centre (2, 1) (c) enlargement, scale factor ½, centre (1, 3)
questions.model: (a) Each image coordinate is double the object's and the lengths double: scale factor 2 from the origin. (b) (2, 1) does not move, so it is the centre; the side 2 becomes 6: scale factor 3.

questions.q: An enlargement maps a 4 cm by 6 cm rectangle to a similar rectangle of area 216 cm². Find the scale factor.
questions.a: 24 cm² → 216 cm² is × 9 = 3², so scale factor 3

questions.q: Explain why the centre of enlargement never moves.
questions.a: Its distance from the centre is 0, and 0 × any scale factor is still 0.

questions.q: To describe an enlargement fully, give:
questions.a: A) the scale factor and the centre
options: the scale factor and the centre

questions.q: The scale factor from 8 cm to 2 cm
Big question: how can you work back to the centre of enlargement?
questions.a: Draw ray lines through each vertex and its image; they meet at the centre.
